The test image shows a corn leaf with circular to oval brown spots surrounded by yellow halos, scattered across the leaf surface. Some spots have tan centers with darker brown margins. This is clearly a leaf disease.

Top candidates based on symptoms: Eyespot, Holcus_Spot, Carbonum_Leaf_Spot, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Tar_Spot, Northern_Leaf_Blight.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely candidates.
Eyespot reference shows many very small spots - much smaller and more numerous than the test image. Not a strong match. Let me check Holcus_Spot.
Holcus spot shows a single pale tan/white spot - different from the darker brown spots in the test image. Let me check Carbonum_Leaf_Spot.
Carbonum leaf spot shows many small lesions but they're more numerous and lack the distinct yellow halos seen in the test image. Let me check Physoderma_Brown_Spot.

Physoderma brown spot shows very small yellowish spots in bands plus dark purplish spots on the midrib. The spots are much smaller and more numerous than the test image. Not a match. Let me check Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback.
Anthracnose shows irregular margin lesions, not circular spots. Not a match. Let me check Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight.
Southern corn leaf blight shows rectangular elongated lesions confined by veins. Not a match. Let me check Tar_Spot.

Tar spot shows small black glossy raised spots - very different. Not a match. I have 1 view remaining. Let me revisit Eyespot with another reference to confirm, since the symptom description (tan spots with brown/purple rings and yellow halos, spots coalescing into necrotic areas) matches the test image well despite the size difference.

All 8 views used. Let me synthesize my analysis.

**Test image features:** Circular to oval brown spots with tan centers, darker brown margins/rings, and prominent yellow halos on a corn leaf. Some spots are coalescing into larger necrotic/chlorotic areas.

**Comparison summary:**
- **Eyespot**: Best match on pattern (tan center + brown ring + yellow halo = classic "eyespot"). KB confirms spots can coalesce into large necrotic areas. Reference spots were smaller but same morphology.
- **Holcus_Spot**: Pale white/tan papery spots, lacks the dark brown ring pattern seen in test image.
- **Carbonum_Leaf_Spot**: Many small lesions without prominent yellow halos.
- **Physoderma_Brown_Spot**: Tiny spots in bands with midrib involvement, different.
- **Anthracnose**: Irregular margin lesions, different shape entirely.
- **Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight**: Rectangular vein-bound lesions, wrong shape.
- **Tar_Spot**: Black raised glossy stromata, completely different.

The concentric ring pattern (tan center, dark brown ring, yellow halo) with coalescing lesions is the hallmark of Eyespot.
